subject: Cloud zone disruption — immediate customer reroute instructions and follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: ops@finco.com, support@acme-retail.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-03-12T08:15:00Z
Subject: Cloud zone disruption — immediate reroute instructions and follow-up

Hi all,

We detected a partial service disruption affecting a subset of cloud zones in US-WEST and EU-CENTRAL starting ~08:00 UTC. Our routing layer is actively failing over most customer traffic automatically, but some of you running strict regional pins or self-managed network policies may see elevated error rates or increased latency.

Short-term four-step mitigation (can be applied in the next 5–15 minutes and should restore >95% of traffic):
1) Console toggle: In Console > Deployments > Traffic Steering, enable the temporary fallback policy called "global-fallback-03" (this forces multi-region routing while we restore zones).
2) Endpoint header: If you control headers, set X-Redwood-Fallback: true for requests to LLM endpoints to allow cross-region routing.
3) DNS/Host: For hard-pinned hostnames, switch to the per-customer fallback host: fallback-us.redwood.ai (us) or fallback-eu.redwood.ai (eu) — see attached reroute_command_snippets.txt for curl examples.
4) Retry/backoff: If you see 429/503, implement exponential backoff with jitter; we recommend initial retry at 200ms, doubling up to 1.6s for user-facing low-latency calls.

We will keep this channel updated. Please reply here if you need a runbook walk-through — we can schedule a 15-min Zoom with SRE.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): reroute_command_snippets.txt (text), regional-fallback-playbook.pdf (pdf)
From: Lisa Park <lisa@finco.com>

Date: 2029-03-12T08:29:00Z
Subject: Re: Cloud zone disruption — immediate reroute instructions and follow-up

Thanks Marissa — quick question: we have a strict VPC peering setup and traffic currently pins to us-west-2. If we flip the Console toggle, will traffic for our service leave the VPC? We cannot route outside our VPC.

Also seeing a handful of 503s on embeddings endpoints (embed-v1) — full error traces attached in our internal ticket.

—Lisa
Platform Ops, FinCo

Date: 2029-03-12T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Cloud zone disruption — immediate reroute instructions and follow-up

Lisa — good call. Short answer: the Console fallback will not break your VPC peering; it only relaxes vendor-side routing and prefers alternate Redwood-managed endpoints that respect existing peering where possible. However, because your deployment is pinned at the region level in our control plane, you should instead apply the header-based approach (recommended) so we can route within your peered regions first. Steps for your team: 

- Apply header X-Redwood-Fallback: true for non-sensitive traffic so our routing can select a peered fallback in eu or another us zone.
- For embeddings (embed-v1): switch to our embed-fallback endpoint (embed-fallback.redwood.ai) for 6–12 hours — it routes to warm standby capacity with identical model weights.

If you’d like, Rishi can join and run the changes with your networking lead.

--
Marissa

Date: 2029-03-13T10:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: Incident note and next actions (for postmortem)

Folks — quick internal summary to capture timeline and owners before formal postmortem: 
- 2029-03-12T07:58 UTC: Cloud provider reported degraded I/O on US-WEST-2 AZ-c and EU-CENTRAL-A, causing increased reconnections in our runtime.
- 2029-03-12T08:15 UTC: Customer-facing notification sent (Marissa).
- 2029-03-12T08:40 UTC: Routing fallback policy global-fallback-03 enabled for affected tenants.
- 2029-03-12T09:20 UTC: Most customers reported restoration; a small set with strict region pins required host swap or header override.
- 2029-03-12T13:10 UTC: Provider completed maintenance window; telemetry shows normalized KV cache hit ratio.

Immediate follow-ups (owners):
- lauren_bishop: Verify console label/UX to make fallback toggles clearer (due 2029-03-20).
- jonas_weber: Run vendor RCA sync to get raw I/O metrics and ask for AZ-level cluster logs (due 2029-03-18).
- rishi_malhotra: Produce per-customer impact report and recommend per-tenant fallback defaults (due 2029-03-15).

I attached the action item tracker (postmortem-action-items.csv). I recommend a customer-facing post-incident note tomorrow with a concise timeline and mitigation steps.

-Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: ops@finco.com, support@acme-retail.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-03-14T16:42:00Z
Subject: Incident follow-up: timeline, impact summary, and preventative steps

Hi Lisa and team,

Thank you for your patience. We completed an internal investigation and here is a concise post-incident update: 

Summary:
- Impact window: 2029-03-12T07:58 UTC to 2029-03-12T13:10 UTC.
- Affected regions: US-WEST (zone c), EU-CENTRAL (zone a), and transient spikes in APAC during provider-side failover.
- Root cause: degraded storage I/O in provider AZs which increased reconnection churn for a subset of runtime hosts; our smart routing normally protected customers but strict region pins prevented automatic full failover for a few tenants.

What we did (mitigation):
- Enabled global-fallback-03 to relax regional pins and routed traffic to warm standby across regions.
- Provisioned additional warm standby capacity for embeddings to reduce cold-start latency.
- Provided per-customer guidance to swap to embed-fallback.redwood.ai and enable X-Redwood-Fallback for minimal disruption.

Preventative actions and timeline:
- Config/UX change: make fallback toggle more visible and add contextual guidance (owner: lauren_bishop, ETA: 2029-03-20).
- Default fallback policy: evaluate making "fallback allowed" the default for tenants below X request threshold to minimize impact of AZ-level disruptions (owner: rishi_malhotra, ETA: 2029-03-15).
- Vendor follow-up: request AZ-level I/O graphs and propose changes to how we pin control plane decisions (owner: jonas_weber, ETA: 2029-03-18).

If you want a tailored impact report for FinCo (per-endpoint error counts, affected keys), Rishi will send that by 2029-03-15. We are also offering a 5% service credit for the impacted time window should you request it — ping me and I’ll route through Renewals.

Apologies for the disruption and thank you for the quick coordination.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): postmortem-action-items.csv
